910.name: Prehistoric and Early Settlement
910.description: The earliest archaeological evidence of habitation in the Macau peninsula, the territory as part of successive Chinese administrations, fishing villages, and the A-Ma Temple's origins.

sub_clusters.name: Neolithic and Chinese Imperial Periphery
sub_clusters.description: Archaeological evidence from Hac Sa and Coloane showing Neolithic habitation, the territory as part of Nanhai Commandery, coastal fishing communities, and the passage of Song dynasty refugees.
key_events: Archaeological sites at Hac Sa Beach reveal evidence of habitation dating to c. 4000 BC

sub_clusters.name: Pre-Portuguese Fishing Village
sub_clusters.description: The establishment of the A-Ma Temple by Fujianese fishermen (from which 'Macau' may derive its name), the territory as a small fishing and incense-trading settlement under Ming Guangdong prefecture.
key_events: A-Ma Temple established — legend holds the goddess Mazu protected fishermen at the site (c. 15th century)

920.name: Portuguese Arrival and Golden Age
920.description: The Portuguese arrival and settlement, Macau as the crucial node in the Lisbon-Goa-Malacca-Macau-Nagasaki trade route, the Jesuit missions to China and Japan, and the golden age of commerce.

sub_clusters.name: Portuguese Settlement and Trade
sub_clusters.description: The Portuguese establishment of a permanent settlement with Ming tacit permission, the lucrative Japan-China silk-for-silver trade, the construction of churches and fortifications, and the Jesuit base for missions to China and Japan.
key_events: Portuguese establish permanent settlement at Macau with tacit Ming permission (1557)
Macau serves as the base for Jesuit missions — Matteo Ricci departs for Beijing (1582)

sub_clusters.name: Dutch Attacks and Japan Trade Loss
sub_clusters.description: The successful defense against Dutch naval attack at the Battle of Macau, the loss of the lucrative Japan trade after the Shimabara Rebellion and sakoku, and the gradual economic decline.
key_events: Battle of Macau — Portuguese and African slave soldiers repel a Dutch invasion fleet (1622)
Japan's sakoku policy cuts Macau off from the Japan trade — devastating the economy (1639)

930.name: Colonial Decline and Opium Era
930.description: Macau's eclipse by Hong Kong, the opium trade, the coolie trade, Portuguese assertion of sovereignty, and the transformation from a prosperous trading post to a colonial backwater.

sub_clusters.name: Eclipse by Hong Kong
sub_clusters.description: The founding of British Hong Kong devastating Macau's commercial position, the opium and coolie trades as controversial revenue sources, and the assertion of Portuguese sovereignty over Taipa and Coloane.
key_events: British Hong Kong's founding eclipses Macau as the major European trading post on the China coast (1842)

sub_clusters.name: Sino-Portuguese Treaty of 1887
sub_clusters.description: Governor Ferreira do Amaral's assertion of Portuguese sovereignty, his assassination, the punitive expeditions, and the 1887 Sino-Portuguese Treaty formally recognizing Portugal's 'perpetual occupation and government' of Macau.
key_events: Governor Ferreira do Amaral asserts Portuguese sovereignty and is assassinated (1849)
Sino-Portuguese Treaty — China recognizes Portuguese sovereignty over Macau (1887)

930.name: Early 20th Century and War Era
930.description: The Portuguese Republic's colonial reforms, the Sun Yat-sen connection, the gambling industry's origins, neutrality during World War II, and Macau's role as a refuge for war refugees.

sub_clusters.name: Gambling Origins and Sun Yat-sen
sub_clusters.description: Sun Yat-sen's early career practicing medicine in Macau, the legalization and monopolization of gambling, the fan-tan houses, and Macau's search for an economic niche in Hong Kong's shadow.
key_events: Sun Yat-sen practices Western medicine in Macau — first Chinese person licensed to do so in the territory (1892)

sub_clusters.name: WWII Neutrality and Refugee Haven
sub_clusters.description: Portuguese neutrality allowing Macau to avoid Japanese occupation, the massive influx of Chinese refugees swelling the population, espionage activity, the famine, and the territory as a haven amid war.
key_events: Macau's population swells from 150,000 to over 500,000 with war refugees (1937–1945)

940.name: Postwar Portuguese Macau
940.description: The postwar colonial stagnation, the 1966 pro-communist riots that shifted power dynamics, the Estado Novo's colonial policies, and Macau's existence in the shadow of both Hong Kong and Communist China.

sub_clusters.name: 12-3 Incident and Political Shift
sub_clusters.description: The December 3rd Incident — Cultural Revolution-inspired riots forcing the Portuguese governor to publicly apologize, effectively ceding political influence to pro-Beijing groups, and transforming Macau's power dynamics.
key_events: 12-3 Incident — Portuguese governor forced to sign humiliating apology to pro-Beijing forces (January 1967)

sub_clusters.name: Carnation Revolution Impact
sub_clusters.description: The 1974 Carnation Revolution in Portugal ending the Estado Novo, the offer to return Macau to China (which Beijing declined), and the reclassification of Macau as a 'Chinese territory under Portuguese administration.'
key_events: Portugal offers to return Macau to China after the Carnation Revolution — Beijing declines (1974)

940.name: Stanley Ho Era and Gambling Monopoly
940.description: Stanley Ho's STDM gambling monopoly transforming Macau's economy, the construction of the Lisboa Casino, the development of tourism infrastructure, and the negotiations for Macau's return to China.

sub_clusters.name: STDM Monopoly and Casino Growth
sub_clusters.description: Stanley Ho's Sociedade de Turismo e Diversões de Macau (STDM) winning the gambling monopoly, the construction of the iconic Hotel Lisboa, hydrofoil ferry services to Hong Kong, and the development of horse and greyhound racing.
key_events: Stanley Ho's STDM wins the Macau gambling monopoly — beginning his 40-year reign as 'King of Gambling' (1962)

sub_clusters.name: Sino-Portuguese Negotiations and Handover Preparation
sub_clusters.description: The Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration agreeing on handover, the drafting of the Macau Basic Law, the localization of the civil service, the new Macau International Airport, and the handover ceremony.
key_events: Sino-Portuguese Joint Declaration — Macau to return to China on December 20, 1999 (April 13, 1987)
Macau handover ceremony — the last European colony in Asia is returned (December 20, 1999)

950.name: Early SAR and Casino Liberalization
950.description: The establishment of the Macau SAR, the revolutionary liberalization of the casino industry, the entry of Las Vegas operators, and Macau's meteoric rise to become the world's gambling capital.

sub_clusters.name: Casino Boom
sub_clusters.description: The end of the STDM monopoly, the entry of Las Vegas Sands, Wynn, and MGM, the Cotai Strip development, Macau surpassing Las Vegas in gambling revenue, and the transformation of the territory's economy and skyline.
key_events: Macau gambling monopoly ended — licenses granted to foreign operators (2002)
Macau's gambling revenue surpasses Las Vegas for the first time (2006)
The Venetian Macao opens on the Cotai Strip — largest casino in the world (2007)

sub_clusters.name: UNESCO Recognition and Heritage
sub_clusters.description: The Historic Centre of Macau inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the preservation of the unique Sino-Portuguese architectural heritage, the Ruins of St. Paul's, and cultural tourism development.
key_events: Historic Centre of Macau inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2005)

960.name: Contemporary Macau
960.description: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign's impact on VIP gambling, economic diversification efforts, the Greater Bay Area integration, COVID-19 border closures, and Macau's evolving relationship with Beijing.

sub_clusters.name: Anti-Corruption Crackdown and Diversification
sub_clusters.description: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption campaign devastating VIP gambling revenue, the push for economic diversification beyond casinos, the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, and integration into the Greater Bay Area.
key_events: Macau gambling revenue drops 34% in 2015 due to Beijing's anti-corruption campaign
Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge opens — world's longest sea-crossing bridge (2018)

sub_clusters.name: COVID-19 and New Gaming Law
sub_clusters.description: The devastating impact of COVID-19 border closures on Macau's casino-dependent economy, the new gaming law increasing government control, the re-tendering of casino concessions, and the push toward the Hengqin cooperation zone.
key_events: COVID-19 border closures virtually halt Macau's tourism — gambling revenue drops 80% (2020)
New gaming law enacted — all six casino operators receive new 10-year concessions (2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
